output.activity: Put 7 spoons on the table. Hide some under a cup while your child looks away, then show what is left, like 2 spoons. Ask how many are under the cup. Lift the cup to check together, then swap turns.

judged.reason: Every count matches the evidence (first-try: 1 each on four Skills plus 2 on Change unknown; Hint: 1 Result unknown and 1 Change unknown; Revealed: 1 Teen numbers and 1 Change unknown), the three kinds of evidence are kept separate, no claims about her thinking are made, and the hidden-spoons activity fits the weakest Skill, Change unknown.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on with a sum of 10 may be shakier than counting-on with other sums. The evidence never singled out a sum of 10. Misses and Hints came with many different sums, and 7 + 3 (p99) and 9 + 1 (p75) were correct on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: No special test needed. Counting-on will keep appearing in ordinary practice with mixed sums.

hypotheses.claim: Teen-number decompose Problems with a larger teen number may be harder than those with a smaller one. The evidence points the other way. 10 + ? = 17 was correct on the first try twice (p98, p106), and 10 + ? = 14 was correct on the first try twice (p116, p128).
hypotheses.nextTest: No further test needed. Teen numbers will still turn up in review.

hypotheses.claim: Take-from-ten Problems with a small number taken away may be less secure than those with a larger number taken away. The test showed the opposite. 10 - 8 (p60, p109), 10 - 4 (p117) and 10 - 7 (p122) were correct on the first try. 10 - 2 was also correct on the first try this Session (p160).
hypotheses.nextTest: No further test needed. Take-from-ten will keep appearing as review.

hypotheses.claim: The compose Problem 10 + 4 = ? was a first-try miss that ended in a Reveal earlier. Later compose Problems were correct on the first try, including 10 + 3 (p91), 10 + 9 (p97) and 10 + 8 (p138). The earlier miss looks like a one-off.
hypotheses.nextTest: No further test needed. Compose Problems will keep appearing in ordinary practice.

hypotheses.claim: The decompose Problem 10 + ? = 12 needed a Hint twice earlier (p25, p39). Later decompose Problems, including 10 + ? = 12 (p73), 10 + ? = 11 (p78) and 10 + ? = 17 (p106), were correct on the first try with no assistance. The earlier difficulty did not repeat.
hypotheses.nextTest: No special test needed. Watch whether teen decompose stays correct on the first try in review.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on Problems in smaller-first form may be less secure than larger-first ones. Earlier both smaller-first Problems needed a Hint (p126, p129) while both larger-first Problems were correct on the first try (p123, p127). Later smaller-first 1 + 12 (p133) was correct on the first try, as was larger-first 12 + 1 (p135). No counting-on Problem came up this Session. The lean rests on Hint-assisted successes and Reveals, and it has weakened.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give counting-on Problems of both structures with matching larger addends (12 to 15) and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten Problems in smaller-first form with a 6 as the first addend may be less secure than other make-a-ten Problems. 6 + 8 needed a Hint (p46), 6 + 7 was a first-try miss that ended in a Reveal (p55), and 6 + 8 was a Reveal again (p81). 9 + 8 in larger-first form was also a Reveal (p88), so trouble is not limited to a 6. Smaller-first 5 + 9 needed a Hint earlier (p118) but was correct on the first try this Session as a review Problem (p154). Smaller-first 3 + 8 was also correct on the first try (p125). Larger-first 7 + 4 (p131), 8 + 8 (p108) and 9 + 5 (p102) were correct on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give make-a-ten Problems with a larger addend of 8 or 9 and with 6 or 7, in both orders, and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Subtraction as unknown addend is unsteady. Earlier misses ended in Reveals or Hints on 6 - 1 (p49), 7 - 6 (p53), 4 - 3 (p56), 7 + ? = 9 (p61), 14 - 12 (p74), 16 - 11 (p87), 9 + ? = 12 (p96) and 14 + ? = 18 (p121). Six first tries in a row were correct (p105 to p111), and 17 - 16 (p124) and 15 - 10 (p136) were correct on the first try. Then 18 - 17 (p152) and 15 - 12 (p159) each needed a Hint. These are Hint-assisted successes, not first-try corrects, and the engine's last two first attempts on this Skill were misses.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give subtract-form unknown-addend Problems with wholes in the teens and a range of missing parts, and check whether first tries stay correct.

hypotheses.claim: Partners to 10 with a given 1 (1 + ? = 10) was a first-try miss that ended in a Reveal (p51), while 3 + ? = 10 (p57), 7 + ? = 10 (p86, p100), 10 - 8 (p109), 10 - 7 (p122), 10 - 1 (p137, p147) and 10 - 2 (p160) were correct on the first try. It looks like a one-off slip.
hypotheses.nextTest: See whether missing-partner Problems with a small given number come up again in review and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Unknown-addend Problems with a whole of 10 may be easier than those with other wholes. 6 + ? = 10 was correct on the first try (p63), while 7 + ? = 9 (p61), 9 + ? = 12 (p96) and 14 + ? = 18 (p121) were first-try misses that ended in Reveals. Many other wholes were correct on the first try (p107, p110, p111, p124, p136). The idea is weak.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give unknown-addend Problems with a whole of 10 and with other wholes, in the same structure, and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Problems with a 9 as a given number may need a Hint or a Reveal more often than others. 9 + ? = 10 (p72), 1 + 9 (p62), 9 + 2 (p42) and 5 + 9 (p118) needed Hints. 9 + 8 (p88) and 9 + ? = 12 (p96) were first-try misses that ended in Reveals. 4 + 9 (p58), 9 + 1 (p75), 3 + 9 (p84), 9 + 5 (p102), 9 - 8 (p150) and 5 + 9 this Session (p154) were correct on the first try. The idea is weakening.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give several Problems with 9 as a given number in make-a-ten, counting-on and unknown-addend, next to similar ones with other numbers, and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Subtract-form unknown-addend Problems where the two numbers are close together may be less secure. 7 - 6 (p53) and 4 - 3 (p56) were Reveals, and 14 - 12 (p74), 18 - 17 (p152) and 15 - 12 (p159) needed Hints. 11 - 9 (p66), 2 - 1 (p69), 16 - 12 (p101) and 17 - 16 (p124) were correct on the first try. Closeness alone does not explain the misses.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give subtract-form unknown-addend Problems with a small missing part and with a bigger missing part, and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Subtract-form and missing-addend-form unknown-addend Problems may differ in how secure they are. In subtract form, 7 - 6 (p53), 4 - 3 (p56) and 16 - 11 (p87) were Reveals and 14 - 12 (p74), 18 - 17 (p152) and 15 - 12 (p159) needed Hints, while many others were correct on the first try, including 17 - 16 (p124) and 15 - 10 (p136). In missing-addend form, 7 + ? = 9 (p61), 9 + ? = 12 (p96) and 14 + ? = 18 (p121) were Reveals, while seven others were correct on the first try. Recent trouble sits in subtract form, but it is not a clear split.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give subtract and missing-addend Problems with similar wholes and missing parts, and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on Problems with a larger addend in the low teens (11 to 14) may be less secure than those with a larger addend of 15. Reveals came on 14 + 3 (p40) and 2 + 11 (p113), and Hints on 3 + 12 (p80), 3 + 13 (p119), 2 + 13 (p126) and 2 + 14 (p129). Many low-teen Problems (p114, p115, p120, p123, p133, p135) and larger ones (p103, p85, p93, p127) were correct on the first try. Size does not explain the misses.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give counting-on Problems with a larger addend of 11 to 14 next to some with 15, in both structures, and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Hints and Reveals may bunch late in a Session. Earlier the first four Problems were correct on the first try, then three of the last four needed a Hint or a Reveal (p118, p119, p121). In another Session the assisted Problems were spread out (p134, p143). Then the last three of eight needed help (p151, p152, p153). This Session the Hints were spread out at positions 4, 6 and 8 (p157, p159, p161), with first-try corrects in between. It is seen in some Sessions, not others.
hypotheses.nextTest: Check whether Hints and Reveals bunch up in the last positions of the next Session, or spread out among the Problems.

hypotheses.claim: Result-unknown add-to Problems with small addends may be unsteady. 4 + 4 (p132), 5 + 2 (p148) and 2 + 3 (p155) were correct on the first try, but 5 + 3 was a first-try miss that ended in a Reveal (p134). It rests on one miss against three first-try corrects.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give several result-unknown add-to Problems with small wholes and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Result-unknown take-from Problems may be less secure when the number taken away is 3 to 5. 8 - 5 (p143) and 6 - 5 (p157) needed Hints, 5 - 4 (p161) needed a Hint, and 4 - 3 was a first-try miss that ended in a Reveal (p151). 2 - 1 (p141), 6 - 1 (p144) and 9 - 8 (p150) were correct on the first try. This rests on first-try misses that were followed by a Hint or a Reveal, and it repeated this Session. The engine's last two first attempts on result-unknown were also misses.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give take-from Problems with a taken-away number of 1 or 2 and of 3 to 5, from wholes 5 to 9, and compare first tries.

hypotheses.claim: Result-unknown take-from Problems where the two numbers are one apart (the result is 1) may be less secure than take-away Problems with a bigger result. 4 - 3 was a Reveal (p151), 18 - 17 needed a Hint (p152), and 6 - 5 and 5 - 4 each needed a Hint this Session (p157, p161). Earlier 4 - 3 (p56) and 7 - 6 (p53) were Reveals. Against that, 9 - 8 (p150), 2 - 1 (p141) and 6 - 1 (p144) were correct on the first try. In take-from-change form, 5 - ? = 4 (p156) and 8 - ? = 1 (p158) were correct on the first try, so the trouble may be tied to the result-unknown form. It rests on Reveals and Hint-assisted successes after first-try misses.
hypotheses.nextTest: Give take-from Problems with wholes 5 to 9, some with a result of 1 and some with a bigger result, next to take-from-change Problems, and compare first tries.

output.activity: Put 6 coins or spoons in a pile. Let your child hide some under a cup while you say how many are left, then ask how many went under the cup. Try it with other starting amounts up to 9.

judged.reason: Every count, the Mastery of Change unknown, and the absence of Reveals and Powers match the evidence, the first-try and after-a-Hint outcomes are kept separate, the note makes no claims about the child's thinking, and the hidden-under-a-cup activity suits the weakest Skill's take-away Problems.
